title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, templates
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and team leads; specific teams may publish supplemental SOPs but must reference and be consistent with these company-level controls.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, clear ownership, and a repeatable onboarding/offboarding process.
Scope: All cloud accounts, internal tools, source repositories, CI/CD, and customer-facing consoles.
Owners: Security (policy), People Ops (onboarding flow), and Team Leads (access approvers).
Key rules:
- Principle of Least Privilege: Grant only the minimum permissions required. Use role-based groups, not user-level grants.
- Approval: All access requests require the requestor, the team lead, and a security reviewer for privileged roles (admins, billing, infra).
- Temporary Access: Use time-limited access (max 7 days) for emergency escalations.
- MFA: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all administrative accounts.
- Periodic Reviews: Teams must run access reviews quarterly; auditors will be notified and findings tracked in the security tracker.
Onboarding checklist (high level):
1. Submit access requests via the Access Portal with justification and duration.
2. Team lead approves and assigns role-group.
3. Security performs privileged role review if applicable.
4. People Ops schedules orientation and confirms tool access.
Deprovisioning: HR triggers offboarding in HRIS; automated workflow revokes cloud and tool access within 4 hours of termination/exit. Exceptions require documented risk acceptance and an owner.

2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce operational risk by standardizing how changes are proposed, reviewed, and rolled out.
Scope: All production-facing services, infra changes (networking, IAM, capacity), and configuration impacting SLOs.
Owners: Eng SRE (process), Eng Platform (rollout tooling), Service Owners (approvals).
SLOs and thresholds: Any change expected to affect availability >1% or latency >20% must follow the formal change window procedure.
Change classifications:
- Standard (low risk) — pre-approved, documented, can be scheduled outside change window.
- Normal — requires RFC and scheduled change window with rollout plan and rollback plan.
- Emergency — follow Emergency Change process; must be logged and reviewed in postmortem within 72 hours.
Required artifacts for Normal change:
- RFC document (purpose, impact, rollback plan, owner, test plan).
- Risk assessment (impact table) and SLO impact estimate.
- Stakeholder approvals (service owner, Eng SRE, product if user-visible).
Deployment controls:
- Use canary and progressive rollouts where applicable (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Automated smoke tests run post-deploy; failure triggers automatic rollback.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect sensitive data, ensure appropriate retention and deletion, and enable data discovery and compliance.
Scope: Customer data, telemetry, logs, backups, model training data.
Owners: Security & Compliance (policy), Data Engineering (platform), Service Owners (data stewards).
Classification:
- Public
- Internal
- Confidential
- Restricted (customer PII, regulated data)
Handling rules:
- Encryption: Data at rest and in transit must be encrypted (TLS 1.2+, AES-256 or equivalent).
- Access: Restricted data requires explicit rationale and privileged access audit logging.
- Retention: Default retention periods are defined in the Data Retention table below; exceptions must be approved by Legal.
Data retention table (defaults):
| Data category | Default retention | Owner |
| Customer telemetry | 24 months | Data Eng |
| Audit logs | 36 months | Security |
| Backups | 90 days | Eng Infra |
| Model training data | 60 months | Research |
Data deletion procedure:
1. Submit deletion request in Data Portal with dataset id and justification.
2. Data steward verifies scope and schedules deletion in maintenance window.
3. Deletion is logged and verified; report generated for compliance.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Centralize purchases for cost control, legal compliance, and vendor visibility.
Scope: Software subscriptions, cloud commitments, hardware purchases, contractor services.
Owners: Finance (policy), Procurement team (execution), Team Budget Owners (approvals).
Approval thresholds:
- <= $5,000: Team lead approval.
- $5,001- $50,000: Dept head + Procurement approval.
- > $50,000: Finance Director + Legal + Procurement committee.
Procurement workflow:
1. Create Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with business justification, SKU, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement sources quotes and negotiates terms (CSP, enterprise discounts).
3. Legal performs contract review for agreements > $50k or handling customer data.
4. Finance issues PO and records commit.
Expense policy highlights:
- Use company card for approved subscriptions under $2,000.
- Personal reimbursements require receipts and submission within 60 days.
- Travel expenses follow the Travel policy below; unapproved expenses may be denied.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Maintain a consistent vendor lifecycle process to manage risk and cost.
Scope: All vendors providing cloud services, software, hardware, or professional services.
Owners: Procurement & Legal (contracting), Security (technical risk), Team owners (operational oversight).
Lifecycle stages:
- Intake: Submit Vendor Intake Form with scope, estimated spend, and data exposure.
- Risk assessment: Security and Legal perform technical and contractual risk reviews.
- Approval: Vendors with access to restricted data require SOC2/ISO27001 or equivalent and a security questionnaire.
- Onboarding: Assign vendor owner, configure accounts/credentials with least privilege, and document contact points and escalation path.
- Review & Renewals: Annual performance and risk review; no auto-renewal for contracts > $50k without review.

6) Travel & Business Expenses
Purpose: Ensure safety, compliance, and predictable spending for business travel.
Scope: All company-sponsored travel and in-person event expenses.
Owners: People Ops (policy), Finance (reimbursements), Security (travel safety guidance).
Booking guidelines:
- Use the approved Travel Portal or travel partners for flights and hotels.
- Economy class for domestic flights under 6 hours; business class requires pre-approval for international flights over 8 hours and senior leadership approval.
Per diem and expense rules:
- Meals up to $80/day domestic, $120/day international; receipts required for > $25 items.
- Ground transportation: use rideshare or company car policy; submit mileage logs for personal car use.
- Subsistence and incidentals follow local tax guidance.
Safety & emergency support:
- Register trips with People Ops for international travel.
- Emergency contact: People Ops travel desk (travel-support@redwood-inference.com) available 24/7.

7) Internal Templates and Required Artifacts
Purpose: Standardize documentation to reduce review friction and speed approvals.
Canonical templates (stored in Templates library):
- Access request form (Access Portal)
- Change RFC template
- Vendor intake form
- Purchase request template
- Data deletion request template
- Travel authorization form
Usage guidance:
- Always attach the relevant template when submitting requests. Incomplete submissions will be returned for clarification.
- Document owners must keep templates updated; major updates require reviewer sign-off and a 14-day communication window before enforcement.
